dropIns.name: Mill Square
dropIns.description: The square where every road in the vale starts, on market day.

dropIns.name: Moor Top
dropIns.description: A knoll above the drove road, with the whole moor ahead of it.

dropIns.name: The Quarry
dropIns.description: The quarry bench under the crag, beside the cliff the Greystone Caves open in.

dropIns.name: Stepping Stones
dropIns.description: By the heron hide at the foot of The Crossing, over the stepping stones from the west bank.

dropIns.name: The Strand
dropIns.description: The strand where the road comes down to the sea.

dropIns.name: Farmhouse
dropIns.description: The yard of the farm at Orchard Terraces, at the top of the terraces.

dropIns.name: The Dam
dropIns.description: The forecourt of the power station, under the dam, with the switchyard gone to grass beyond it.

dropIns.name: Rest House
dropIns.description: The rest house in the middle of the reserve, the dry ground a raid stops at.

dropIns.name: Salvage Camp
dropIns.description: The salvage camp on the beach under the east cape, with the wreck out on the reef.

dropIns.name: Old Quay
dropIns.description: The quay of the drowned port, where the jetty from the strand comes in.

dropIns.name: Cove Steps
dropIns.description: The cliff top over the cove, where the steps go down.

people.name: Trader
lines: Fresh from the orchards over the river. Well. Over the road.
The road east takes you on to The Crossing.

people.name: Ada
lines: There is a cave up in the peaks. Mum says it goes all the way to the sea.

people.name: Pip
lines: Race you to the fountain!
I always win. Ada says that does not count because I start closer.

people.name: Old Peg
lines: Everything on that stall was cheaper before you got here.
Everything was cheaper before anybody got here.

people.name: Stallholder
lines: Apples from the orchard, down the lane past the brook.
Or pick them yourself. Everybody else does.

people.name: Miller
lines: The pond turns the wheel all year. It would be nice if it paid as well.
The brook runs right through the village and comes out at Tom’s pool.

people.name: Old Wick
lines: Nothing in this pond but Magikarp and regret.
Mind, if you have a rod, press at the water. It costs you nothing but time.

people.name: Carter
lines: I lost my purse somewhere round this yard. Do not tell the board.
It told everyone.

people.name: Grandpa Ott
lines: This is the oldest cottage in the vale.
When I was a boy there was snow on the peaks all summer.

people.name: Digger
lines: Dig, plant, chase off the Oddish. Dig, plant, chase off the Oddish.
It is a living. It is not a good one.

people.name: Mrs Marlow
lines: I grow beans. Ott says he grows beans. Those are not beans.

people.name: Fern
lines: There is a garden behind the woodcutter’s, walled off by one small tree.
Old Hazel left it. Nobody with a Cut has been past in years.

people.name: Nan Birch
lines: Sit down, you look terrible.
Everybody who comes through here looks terrible. It is the raids.

people.name: Bram
lines: My mum says never to go down to the pool on your own.
Tom goes down there on his own. Tom is ten.

people.name: Gardener
lines: Every Pidgey in the vale nests in my roof.
East of the village the road goes over the bridge at The Crossing.

people.name: Mrs Lark
lines: Best in show, nine years running. There is no show. I started it. I judge it.

people.name: Lost Walker
lines: Is this the way to the marsh? I have been going round this tree for some time.
South, you say. Down the lane. Yes. Obviously.

people.name: Drover
lines: That Tauros has walked off this moor and back four times this year.
Up the road, mind the ledges. They only go down.

people.name: Gatekeeper
lines: I keep the gate. There is no gate. It is a very quiet job.
East: The Crossing, and the only bridge for miles.
calls: Mind the gate. There is none.

people.name: Wayfarer
lines: The Westward Road goes out of the vale, if you need to go out in a hurry.
Most people who come through do.

people.name: Picker
lines: The berries grow back by the next raid. Do not ask me how. I just pick.

people.name: Woodcutter
lines: A proper axe would clear that little tree by the garden in one go.
I have a blunt one and a bad back. You want a Pokemon that knows Cut.

people.name: Tom
lines: The pool is full of Magikarp!
Nobody believes me. There is something on the island too. Mind the gaps.

people.name: Miller’s Boy
lines: Mind the sacks. I have counted them. I am going to count them again.
The wheel has not stopped in eighty years. Nobody knows how to stop it.

people.name: Nurse
lines: The machines are spoken for, I am afraid. There is a raid on, you know.
If you are hurt, the pump on the green has medicine by it. Nobody counts it.

people.name: Clerk
lines: Sorry, nothing on the shelves till the boat comes in.
Professor Oak’s parcel? We sent it out by the lane. It will be lying about somewhere.

people.name: Mrs Ott
lines: He told you about the snow, did he.
There was no snow.

people.name: Drover Boy
lines: Grandad says they know the way home.
They do. They go there. All the time. Without me.

people.name: Lina
lines: I count them every time and get a different number.
I got six once. There were never six.

people.name: Tarn Fisher
lines: Up on the moor the water has nothing in it but sky.
I come for the quiet. Well. I did.

people.name: Peak Walker
lines: East is the quarry, and the caves under it. Mind who you meet in there.
I have been meaning to go. I have been meaning to go for years.

people.name: Walker
lines: Going up? You will not get down the way you came, not by the ledges. They only go one way.
Quick, mind. Very quick.

people.name: Shepherd
lines: The tarn never freezes, whatever the winter.
There was a sheep track west, under it, to the old chapel.
By day the fog turns you back. Go after dark, if you go.

people.name: Shepherd’s Lad
lines: Grandad says they are sheep. They have horns and they are poisonous.
I asked when we might get a sheep. He went very quiet.

people.name: Toll Clerk
lines: Nobody has paid the toll in forty years, but I still have to write it down.
That is nobody, again. You are the fourth nobody today.

people.name: Mother Stone
lines: They sing at night, the stones. Clefairy come up to hear it.
I have counted them twice tonight. Nine and eleven. It is a good sign, or the other thing.

people.name: Drover’s Wife
lines: You touch the Grey Stones for luck, going up and coming down.
He touched them every time for thirty years. Then a Tauros sat on him. So.

people.name: Camp Cook
lines: It is stew. It has been stew since Tuesday. It will be stew until we reach the sea.
There is more in it now than there was. I do not ask.

people.name: Herd Girl
lines: This fold holds sixty. We had sixty. I shut the gate myself.
There are fifty-nine, and one in Millbrook. I do not understand how he does it.

people.name: Mrs Alder
lines: Three weeks I have taken these waters, for my nerves.
They taste of egg. I am very nervous about it.

people.name: Attendant
lines: Three cups before breakfast, three after, and a brisk walk to the bench.
It has never cured anybody, but they do sit very nicely.

people.name: Colonel
lines: Bad leg. Other one is worse. Took the waters at Pewter in my day.
East of here is the quarry, and the caves. Do not. Well. I did. Look at my leg.

people.name: Trail Boy
lines: I carry water down to Millbrook for people who cannot come up.
It is mostly just water from the pump, by the time I get there. Do not tell them.

people.name: Old Hob
lines: A boulder came down in my grandad’s day and the fold was shut and everybody forgot.
I did not forget. I just live here now. It is very quiet. Thank you for moving it.

people.name: Clerk’s Mother
lines: Forty years of ledgers in this house and not a penny in any of them.
He does lovely handwriting.

people.name: Shepherd’s Wife
lines: He went up after a lost one on a night raid once, along the track to the old chapel.
He came back. He does not go up at night now. He does not say why. Nor does the dog.

people.name: Tarn Fisher
lines: Coldest water in the vale. A fish that lives in this is not in the mood to be caught.
I have been here since before the river was. I started it, for all you know.

people.name: Sketcher
lines: I am painting the tarn. It has been raining in the painting for three weeks.
It is not raining here. That is just how it has turned out.
calls: Do not move. Oh, you moved.

people.name: Bothy Keeper
lines: Nobody owns the bothy. I just happen to have been here since the war, and I do the kettle.
If you came up past the tarn you are halfway. Halfway to what depends on the fog.

people.name: Cloud Watcher
lines: There is a summit up there. Stormcrown. You can see it two days a year, and I have seen it once.
There is no way up from this side. They say the only road to it starts at the very bottom of the caves.
calls: It might clear in a minute.

people.name: Rock Picker
lines: It is all the same rock. People pay for it anyway. I do not tell them.
Further up it is the same rock again, and colder.

people.name: Climber
lines: The river is born in this tarn. Follow it down and you come to The Crossing.

people.name: Ganger
lines: Thirty years we have been widening this cutting. It is getting narrower.
Nobody can tell me why. I have stopped asking the rock.

people.name: Navvy
lines: Dig, carry, tip. Dig, carry, tip. The Machop does the carrying.
I have asked what I am for. They said digging. The Machop digs too.

people.name: Pony Girl
lines: They come up here for the summer. I come up here because they will not come down.
Shut the gate when you go. That one knows how to open it, but it likes to be asked.

people.name: Lamp Seller
lines: Lamps. Two for the price of three. You would be amazed how many people go in without one.
You would not be amazed how many come out. Top floor down from here, and it gets worse.

people.name: Foreman
lines: Every step in Millbrook came off this bench, and every statue at The Crossing.
Somebody left a good crate of tools up here and has not been back. Big lad. Very serious.

people.name: Quarryman
lines: You hit it till it breaks. Then there are two of it. Then you hit that.
Thirty years in, and there is more of it than when I started.

people.name: Stone Carter
lines: Going down full, coming up empty. You would think that was the easy way round.
That is what the last horse thought.

people.name: Carter’s Lad
lines: That Mankey up on the edge throws things at the carts. It has got a very good arm.
I threw one back. It kept it.

people.name: Goat Boy
lines: These are my goats. They are very good goats. Mum says they are Rhyhorn.
I have told them. They do not mind.

people.name: Mountain Ranger
lines: Lost on the hill? The Goat Track leaves through the pasture, west of the gorge.
Everybody who comes down that pass is sure they know the way. I have a very good chair.

people.name: Mrs Gantry
lines: Rope? I have got rope. I have got tea, if you do not want rope.
Everybody who goes up that pass wants rope on the way back. They never think of it on the way up.

people.name: Tally Clerk
lines: Tons out: forty thousand. Tons left: all of it.
I have sent the figures to Millbrook. They have asked me to stop.

people.name: Old Wren
lines: Nobody signs the trails in Pine Hollow. You find them or you do not.
The deer go south out of the hollow, down to the broadleaf wood.

people.name: Water Girl
lines: Coldest spring in the vale. Gran says it cures everything.
She says that about everything. I just carry it.

people.name: Col Walker
lines: Over the col from the peaks and this is what you get. Trees.
There is a charcoal track goes out of the nook south of here, if you know it. I never told you.

people.name: Old Collier
lines: My stack went cold here in the year of the fire. It has never been the same since.
You go out that way, behind me, if anything comes through the pines after you.

people.name: Resin Tapper
lines: Cut the bark, hang the pot, come back in a year. This whole wood weeps if you ask it.
Leave it a very long time, and it goes to amber. There is a collector down at the harbour who pays silly money.

people.name: Tapper’s Girl
lines: There is a Caterpie stuck in one of the old lumps, right the way through. Dad says a thousand years.
I said sorry to it.
calls: Do not touch, it is sticky!

people.name: Amber Hunter
lines: That pine has been weeping since before there was a vale. Look under it. Look under all of them.
Amber lies anywhere in this wood. Good luck finding it twice.

people.name: Bee Warden
lines: Those are not bees. I keep saying that. They have got my hat.
It is a very big nest. Do not stand there. No. Do not stand there either.

people.name: Linesman
lines: I walk the cable from the station to the pass, and the Pikachu sit on it and drink.
I had a card for the Service Gate. I had it when I passed the oak. If you find it, you never saw me.

people.name: Collier’s Mate
lines: Bram does not talk. He has not said anything since the spring.
He said something to you? Sit down. Tell me everything.

people.name: Walked Off
lines: Nine years on that picket, and one morning I went for a walk. Do not tell them where I am.
I am not telling you where this road goes, either. You would only tell them.

people.name: Pot Carrier
lines: Two pots for the tappers. They said I would find the camp. They said it the way people do here.
Nobody tells you anything in Pine Hollow, and then they ask why you are late.

people.name: Deer Stalker
lines: Eleven years I have stalked the deer of Pine Hollow. I have seen the path, the prints, the droppings.
South out of the hollow, then on down. There is a very fine wood at the bottom of it, I am told.

people.name: Old Wren’s Sister
lines: She told you nothing. She tells everybody nothing. She has been telling me nothing for seventy years.
The oak glade is east. There. Now you know as much as I do.

people.name: Carter
lines: Everything Millbrook sells comes over that bridge, and I have carried all of it.
My back would like a word with the people who built a village on the wrong side of a river.

people.name: Ostler
lines: That Ponyta bites. No, it does not. It burns. I do not know why I said bites.

people.name: Withy Cutter
lines: Baskets, hurdles, the odd eel trap. It all comes out of this bed.
Your lane there runs down to the stones. Keep your feet.

people.name: Mason
lines: It was going to be the Mayor of Millbrook. Then he stopped paying.
Now it is nobody in particular. It is coming on very well.

people.name: Stone Carter
lines: Up the road for stone, down the road for stone. Up, down.
Some of those are stones. Some of those are Geodude. They are paid the same.

people.name: Angler
lines: Biggest thing in this river is the one my brother did not catch.
I did not catch one nearly as big. Press at the water with a rod, if you have one.

people.name: Brother
lines: He told you about the fish. There was a fish. It was this big.
I show him this big, every year. He has never once believed it.

people.name: Toll Keeper
lines: The bridge is free. It has been free for ninety years. I keep it free.
Somebody has to. You would be surprised how much it costs.

people.name: Stall Girl
lines: Everything here came over that bridge one way, and it is going back the other.
It is cheaper on the way back. Nobody knows why. Do not tell them.

people.name: Stallholder
lines: Honey from the bees, stone from the peaks, eels from the marsh. And me.
I am the only thing here that came from nowhere.

people.name: Lad
lines: East is Tanglewood. Everybody who goes in says it is easy.
Then you see them a day later coming out the other side, very quiet.

people.name: Pip’s Aunt
lines: My nephew in Millbrook says he always wins.
I raced him at Christmas. He started very close.

people.name: Old Drover
lines: Sixty head from the moor to the sea and I lost but the one.
He is in Millbrook. He has a pound of his own now. He has done very well.

people.name: Peddler
lines: East is Tanglewood. I go round it, myself.
Folk who leave that road come out a day later.

people.name: Beekeeper
lines: You tell them everything, bees. Who has married, who has died. They like to know.
I told them about you. They were not interested. Mind the big one.

people.name: Heron Man
lines: A heron can stand still for six hours. I have timed it.
I timed it from here. It took six hours.

people.name: Weir Keeper
lines: The eels come down in autumn, all at once, in the dark, off to the sea.
Nobody has ever seen them come back. They come back, though. Nobody knows how. Eels.

people.name: Burner
lines: You keep it covered and you keep it slow. Six days and you do not sleep.
Then you have got charcoal, and nobody thanks you. Mind the Vulpix. It likes to help.

people.name: Burner’s Wife
lines: Everything I own smells of smoke. That is why I married him. It was the smell or nothing.

people.name: Innkeeper
lines: The coach went into the river in my grandfather’s day. The Ponyta swam out.
We have kept the name. We have kept the Ponyta. It has a room.

people.name: Traveller
lines: Six of us came over the bridge. Five of us are staying for dinner.
I did not ask.

people.name: Pedlar’s Wife
lines: He is out there telling people he goes round Tanglewood.
He got lost in it in the spring. He was gone a week. Do not tell him I told you.

people.name: Keeper’s Wife
lines: He has not taken a penny on that bridge in thirty years, and he is out there every day.
I married a very honest man. I would not recommend it.

people.name: Watcher
lines: There is a slot in the wall for looking at the herons through, and they know about it.
They stand just out of the slot. I have started to take it personally.

people.name: Woodman
lines: We only cut the edge. Nobody who went in to cut the middle has sent any wood back.
Keep to the road. I know everybody says it. Keep to it anyway.

people.name: Young Woodman
lines: There was a deer path here somewhere, just off the road. It comes out at a gap.
If you ever need to leave in a hurry. Which you will. People do.

people.name: Sawyer
lines: One man on top of the log, one man down the pit. I am the man down the pit.
You get a lot of sawdust and a very low opinion of the man on top.

people.name: Picnic Mum
lines: We said we would just go in as far as the pond.
This is as far as the pond. Nobody is to go any further. Tim. TIM.

people.name: Tim
lines: There is a lane behind that tree that goes all the way to a statue. I saw it.
I saw it from a very long way away. I am not allowed.

people.name: Picnic Dad
lines: I know exactly where we parked the cart.
It is just a question of which way we were facing when I knew it.

people.name: Mushroom Woman
lines: Every lane in this wood is the same lane. I have been picking along it for sixty years.
Do not stand in the ring. Paras lives there, and it thinks it owns the place. It does.
calls: Not that one. Not that one.

people.name: Lost Picnicker
lines: I took one turn off the road for a picnic spot.
That was this morning.

people.name: Old Founder
lines: I took one turn off the road in the year of the big snow. So did she, and him.
We put up a hut for the night. That was the hut.
Mislaid. Population fourteen. Founded by accident, and nobody has apologised.

people.name: Mrs Turner
lines: We are leaving in the morning. We have got it all worked out this time.
I have said that for nineteen years, and I have got a very nice garden out of it.

people.name: Postman
lines: I have a letter for Bridge End. It was urgent, in my father’s day.
I can see the smoke from there, some mornings. I wave the letter at it.

people.name: Dot
lines: I was born here. What is a road?
Grandad says it is like a lane that means it. I do not think he is well.

people.name: Gardener
lines: Best soil in the vale. Nobody has ever come back to complain.

people.name: Surveyor
lines: I came to map this wood for the Crown, you know. Here is the map.
It is a very good map of here. I have not been anywhere else to compare it.

people.name: Shrine Keeper
lines: It was a shrine to something. We have lost the name of it.
We keep it up anyway, in case it remembers us.

people.name: Pilgrim
lines: I walked three days to ask it the way home.
It is very good about listening. It has not said anything yet.

people.name: Pilgrim’s Lad
lines: Gran says the old stones go underground, at the rock, past the camp.
She says the keepers used to go in. She does not say whether they came out.

people.name: Caver
lines: This is the Wood Mouth. Greystone Caves, second floor, by the time you are in.
There is a way down from here to the sea and a way up to the quarry. We have lost two ropes finding out.

people.name: Tea Woman
lines: They go in, I keep the kettle on. They come out, I count them.
It has never yet been the same number. I have stopped telling them.

people.name: Pedlar
lines: Halfway, it says. Everybody stops here and feels better about it.
Nobody has ever asked halfway to what. Pins?

people.name: Hermit Bracken
lines: I came out here to get away from people, and I have never met so many.
Directions are one Potion. They are all wrong. It keeps people from coming back.

people.name: Carter Yeo
lines: Stopped to ask the way. Eleven days ago. A wheel came off while I was asking.
East is the Safari Marsh, if you are going. They have got a proper gate. They would.
calls: You got a wheel on you?

people.name: Carter’s Boy
lines: We were carrying turnips. We are carrying less turnips now.
Do not tell him about the Rattata. He thinks it is the damp.

people.name: Ned
lines: Members catch and release. That is the rule. Release is optional. That is also the rule.
Tam says everybody gets lost in here, and that is how he catches them. Tam is not well.
calls: Got one! No I have not.

people.name: Nell
lines: It was a Caterpie on Tuesday. Then it was a Metapod and it did not do anything for a week.
Then it was a Butterfree and it left. I cried. Do not tell Ned.

people.name: Woodcutter
lines: Lost? Every path in Tanglewood comes back to the road in the end.
I was sent to cut this one down. I have been working up to it for thirty years.

people.name: Acorn Girl
lines: Every acorn off this tree goes in the bag. In the bag, in the wood, and up comes a pine.
I do not know why. Nobody has ever seen another oak come up. I just keep trying.

people.name: Forester
lines: I keep the official map of Tanglewood. Every year I go out and correct it.
Every year the wood has moved. Trees are not meant to do that. I have written to them.

people.name: Picker Joss
lines: These got away from the farm, years back. Sour as anything.
Farmer Hale says they are still his. The trees have not been told. South is the Pickers’ way down.

people.name: Quarryman
lines: We broke into this from the quarry above.
Every ladder in here goes down. To cross the vale you go down and come up again.

people.name: Camper Lin
lines: I followed the bats down from the wood.
Now every passage looks like the last one.

people.name: Lost Hiker
lines: This floor is two caves with a wall of rock between.
To get to the other side you go down a floor and back up. I have done it twice.

people.name: Miner
lines: Listen. That rushing is the sea, three floors down.

people.name: Old Miner
lines: We called it the Sleeper.
An Onix, in the east sand. It was lying there before the quarry was dug.

people.name: Fisherman
lines: The tide comes up the passage from the strand.
The Shellder ride in on it and stay.

people.name: Landlord
lines: Everybody who comes in asks if this is the way out. Every one of them, and then they laugh.
Then they stop laughing, and then they have a drink. It is a good living.

people.name: Regular
lines: I only came in to ask the way.
That was before the old king died. Which old king? Exactly.

people.name: Lost Salesman
lines: I had an appointment in Millbrook at ten.
I think I can still make it, if nobody stops me having this one.

people.name: Club Secretary
lines: The club has eleven members and four hundred and six Weedle, and only the Weedle pay their dues.
Mostly in Poison Sting.

people.name: Forester’s Wife
lines: Every wall in here is the map of that wood, and no two of them agree.
He went out to look at the east lanes in the spring. He says it was yesterday.

people.name: Thatcher
lines: Half of Millbrook sleeps under this marsh. It keeps the rain off, mostly.
If you are in a hurry, do not wade. It only feels quicker.

people.name: Reed Boy
lines: I carry the bundles up to the yard. Then they give me more bundles.
That is the whole job. I thought there would be more to it.

people.name: Wildfowler
lines: Sit very still on this bank and the whole marsh comes to you.
Then a raider wades through and it all goes home again.

people.name: Old Bittern
lines: Sixty years I have come out here and I have shot nothing.
I do not own a gun. I just like the hat.

people.name: Mere Fisher
lines: Still as a plate, this mere. I have fished it forty years.
Nothing yet.

people.name: Pond Boy
lines: This pond is not on the map. I checked. So it is mine.
You can look. Looking is free. Fishing is one Poké Ball. Nobody has paid yet.

people.name: Lock Keeper
lines: I open the sluice when the water comes up and shut it when it goes down.
Nobody has told me what happens if I stop. I am not going to be the one who finds out.

people.name: Reed Cutter
lines: We cut the reeds for thatch.
Wade through them if you like. The boardwalk is longer, but you stay dry.

people.name: Tadpole Nan
lines: There are eleven frogs. I have named them all Gerald.
The big one is Big Gerald. He will fight you. He fights everybody.

people.name: Old Seth
lines: My father ran this pump, and his father. It has not pumped anything since the rain.
I still oil it. You do not stop oiling a thing just because it has stopped.
calls: She will go again one day.

people.name: Puntman
lines: Punt goes out to Duck Island and comes back. Walk to the end of the boards and press on.
No, there is nothing out there. Nothing you can eat. There is a hermit. He is not for eating either.

people.name: Eel Wife
lines: Eels go up the drain at night. You can hear them, if you have nothing else to do.
I have nothing else to do.

people.name: Hermit Moss
lines: I came out here to be alone with my thoughts.
There were not as many as I had hoped.
Something is dug in under my good tree. It came with the island. I never looked.

people.name: Eel Seller
lines: Smoked is the good one. Jellied is the one I have got most of.
If you have a rod, the bay is full of them. Please do not. It is my living.

people.name: Mrs Pike
lines: Last winter the bay came up through my floor and took the good chair.
We got it back. It was in the Drowned Duck. They said it floated in.

people.name: Wren
lines: I can swim to the island. Mum says I cannot. I can, though. I just have not.

people.name: Netmaker
lines: Every net in the vale came out of that loft, and every hole in them came out of the Krabby.
Down the coast they pay double. Down the coast they have Krabby.

people.name: Smoker
lines: You smell of smoke now. You will always smell of smoke now.
It is a good smell. You will not get a table anywhere, mind.

people.name: Turf Cutter
lines: Peat is just a marsh that gave up. Cut it, dry it, burn it.
It takes a thousand years to grow a spade of it. I do about four hundred a day.

people.name: Turf Boy
lines: Dad says those Diglett do more than I do.
They do. They are very good. They do not take a wage. I have spoken to them about it.

people.name: Birder Tess
lines: Hush. The ducks only come in when nobody wades the reeds.
One of those has not moved in a week. I am beginning to think it is a Lapras doll.

people.name: Mrs Osier
lines: Baskets for the eels, baskets for the peat, baskets to put the other baskets in.
My sister at The Crossing says hers are better. They are not. Do not tell her I said so.

people.name: Old Reeve
lines: I collected the toll on the Mere Path for thirty years. There is no toll now.
I still sit here. Somebody ought to.
West, and do not stop for anybody on the path. Nobody good is out there.

people.name: Snipe Shooter
lines: You have walked all this way into the reeds to talk to me. I do not know what to do with that.
Nobody comes up here. That is what it is for.

people.name: Birdwatcher
lines: Birdwatching. That is what I am doing. With these crates. Which are for birds.
Cove? What cove? There is no cove down that path. Very rocky, the no cove.

people.name: Landlady
lines: Beds are full. Beds are always full. There are two of them.
The duck is not for looking at. It is stuffed. It is a very sad story and it costs extra.

people.name: Old Soak
lines: There is a hermit on that island owes me eleven years of ale.
Tell him I said hello. Tell him I said eleven.

people.name: Eel Man
lines: Same seat, same pint, forty years. I have asked them to move the door, it lets the bay in.
They have asked me to move.

people.name: Young Pike
lines: Mum says we have to keep the door shut or the bay gets in.
It got in anyway. Look at the floor.

people.name: Net Mender
lines: Every hole in every net in the vale comes through this room.
You would not believe the holes. I have seen a hole that was mostly hole.

people.name: Old Ness
lines: The boats go out from the end of the jetty.
There is a cave under the cliffs. The tide hides it.

people.name: Beachcomber
lines: Everything the sea takes off the wreck ends up in this cove.
Mind the Krabby. They think it is theirs.

people.name: Fisherman
lines: The Magikarp come up from the sea this far, and no further.

people.name: Kite Flyer
lines: The wind off the sea takes my kite right over the cliffs!
That is four kites. There is a very well-off Krabby down there.

people.name: Old Bertie
lines: Lit her every night for forty years, and nobody has told me to stop.
They did tell me. I did not catch it. My hearing is very selective.

people.name: Ropemaker
lines: Forty fathoms a day, walking backwards. I have not seen where I was going since I was twelve.
If that Mankey has the end of it again, I am not going to know until the far post.
calls: Mind your back. Mine, I mean.

people.name: Rope Boy
lines: I turn the wheel. He walks away. Then I turn the wheel some more. He is nearly at Pewter.

people.name: Sexton
lines: There is nobody under most of these. The sea keeps them. These are just where to come and shout.
I have got a good one for you, down in the far corner. He is not dead. He owes me for the stone.

people.name: Salt Raker
lines: Sea goes in, sun comes out, sea goes away, you rake what is left.
Everything tastes of it. My wife tastes of it. It is a very nice marriage.

people.name: Net Wife
lines: Every boat out of this strand has got one of my nets on it, and every net has got a hole.
They say I do not mend them. I say they keep finding Krabby.

people.name: Drying Rack Dan
lines: Salt, wind and three days on the rack. Then you could mend a boot with it.
People have. Those boots are very well thought of.

people.name: Fishwife
lines: Fresh in this morning. Which morning, I could not swear to.
If it looks back at you, that is how you know.

people.name: Fisher Lad
lines: I went on the boat once. Out to the end of the jetty.
They say past that there are islands. They say there is ice on one, and on the other a mountain on fire.
I think they say that to get you on the boat.

people.name: Stage Angler
lines: Good bit of stage, this. Tide comes up through the boards at the spring.
Press at the water with a rod, if you have one. There is a Tentacool I am not speaking to.

people.name: Gorse Burner
lines: Burn it back every spring or the whole heath goes to gorse.
It goes to gorse anyway. It is very good at it. I am quite fond of it.

people.name: Salt Carter
lines: Salt to the boats, fish to the salt, boats to the fish. I have been up and down this hill all my life.
I got to The Crossing once. It was all right.

people.name: Wracker
lines: Three crates this week, and one of them full of dolls. What is it with that ship and dolls?
Something is under the sand by that log. I keep meaning to dig, but it might be somebody’s.

people.name: Wracker’s Girl
lines: I found a boot. Then I found another boot. They are not the same boot.
I am going to keep looking until I find somebody with one of each.

people.name: Courting Couple
lines: You can see the whole coast from up here. Yes. That is why we come. The coast.

people.name: Bertie’s Niece
lines: We have told him. We have told him in writing. He uses it to light the lamp.

people.name: Old Skipper
lines: Forty years I fished off that strand and I have never yet seen the Mere Punt come out to sea.
It is a very small boat. They are very sensible.

people.name: Mrs Sprat
lines: The lower town was my mother’s. You can see her roof, at low water, off the end of the jetty.
We did not sell it. It sort of went.

people.name: Farmer Hale
lines: Hop the terraces if you are in a hurry. Mind, you will not climb back.
Those trees up in the wood are mine, and I will have them back one day. Tell them.

people.name: Hen Girl
lines: These are the hens. There are nine and they have two heads each, so that is eighteen.
They lay one egg between them, and they argue over whose it is.

people.name: Barn Hand
lines: Apples in the store, hay in the barn, and Himself in a mood.
That medicine bag on the shelf belongs to some nurse down the harbour. It came up with the vet.

people.name: Mrs Hale
lines: I grow the beans, I feed the hands, and I do the books. He says he runs the farm.
It is very good for him to think so.

people.name: Picker
lines: These are the old trees. The best apples are always the highest ones.
Which is why I am down here telling you about them.

people.name: Old Picker
lines: Fifty harvests. I can tell you the tree by the taste, and the year by the tree.
Nobody has ever asked.
calls: Not that one. It is thinking.

people.name: Cowman
lines: That one is Buttercup. That one is also Buttercup. It saves time.
Do not stand behind a Tauros, or in front. Stand somewhere else, on another farm.

people.name: Scarecrow
lines: It does not answer. It is a scarecrow. It was facing the other way a minute ago.

people.name: Shepherd
lines: Rough grazing. We tried sheep, but something kept eating them. We tried something else.
It ate that as well. Hop the ledges down, it is quicker than walking.

people.name: Apple Girl
lines: Pip says I am not to take any. Pip says that about everything.
I have told him it is not his orchard. It is not. It is just his apples.

people.name: Cider Maker
lines: Everything goes in. Windfalls, wasps, the odd boot. It all comes out as cider.
It is very good for you. It is very good at something.

people.name: Honest Tom
lines: I am not watching the box. Nobody watches the box. That is the whole idea of it.
I just happen to sit here. All day. Looking at it.
calls: I saw nothing. I saw that.

people.name: Herdsman
lines: That pond has not gone down in a dry year or come up in a wet one. Sit and watch it.
I have. The Tauros have. Nothing happens, and it is the best part of the day.

people.name: Shell Digger
lines: The tide leaves the best shells right at the far end of the sands!
I found a whole boot once. Dad is wearing it.

people.name: Cockle Woman
lines: You rake them at low water and you get off the sand at the turn. It comes in faster than you.
There is a path up through the wood at the west end. Everybody here has run up it.

people.name: Cockle Lad
lines: Nan can tell when the tide will turn from the smell.
I can tell from when it is round my knees.
calls: Nan! It is at my knees!

people.name: Boatman
lines: One boat. We use it for going out and for coming back.
Down the coast there is a very quiet cove, I am told. Very good fishing. Very expensive fish.

people.name: Gran Hale
lines: Sit down. You look thin. Everybody who comes through here looks thin, and I blame the raids.
The Pokémon Center sent a girl for that medicine bag. We fed her. She went home in the end.

people.name: Hungry Picker
lines: Dinner is at twelve. It is not twelve. I am going to stand here until it is.

people.name: Sleeping Hand
lines: Zzz... the hay... the hay is finished, Mr Hale... zzz...

people.name: Cowman’s Wife
lines: He calls me Buttercup as well. I have asked him to stop. He has asked me which one I am.

people.name: Taster
lines: Somebody has to. I took it on for the good of the farm.
Forty years of that. Have I told you about the farm? Lovely farm. Have I told you?

people.name: Shop Steward
lines: Nine years out, and not one of us has crossed this line. Solidarity, that is.
Management? Went home in the flood. We have sent them a very strongly worded letter.

people.name: Picket
lines: We want the turbines back on. Then we want to not turn them on until they say sorry.
I do not know if anybody has thought that through.

people.name: Picket
lines: My mum was on this line. My nan brought the sandwiches. I got my union card for my fifth birthday.

people.name: Scab
lines: I go in every morning and dust. Somebody has to, and it is very quiet in there.
There is something on the turbine floor. It is yellow. I dust round it.

people.name: Meter Man
lines: Nought volts. Nought volts. Nought volts. Something bit me. Nought volts.
The Company asks for these figures every month. Well, it did.

people.name: Mrs Watt
lines: That marrow of mine would have been a yard long if somebody had not breathed on it.
I know who. He knows I know. We have not spoken since the year of the flood.

people.name: Mr Ampere
lines: I do not measure her marrow. I happen to walk past it, with a tape.
It is the water, you know. Out of the tailrace. Everything comes up very big, and warm.

people.name: Terrace Lad
lines: My dad says there will be lights again one day.
I have never seen lights. Are they good?

people.name: Terrace Mum
lines: Nine years on half pay from a Company that does not exist.
It still comes, mind. In an envelope. I have stopped looking at who sends it.

people.name: Company Clerk
lines: We are open. We have always been open. We have no goods, and you would need tokens.
I can offer you a very nice receipt.

people.name: Commodore
lines: Commodore of the Club, since the last one drowned. In a manner of speaking. He moved to the coast.
There is the one dinghy. Take it. Nobody sails. We only come for the bar.

people.name: Crew
lines: Rowed it out to the tower last spring. There is a chap out there. He asked me what year it was.
I told him. I wish I had not. He went very quiet and turned the wheel.

people.name: Valve Man
lines: Half a turn on the hour. Nobody has relieved me, so I have not been relieved.
If I stop, you see, I do not know what happens. That is rather why I have not stopped.

people.name: Apprentice
lines: First day. They told me to wait here for the foreman. I am not sure which year he meant.
That mast still works. Nobody is on the other end, but it hums when you ask it nicely.

people.name: Long Walker
lines: I am walking the whole of the Pylon Road, end to end. There are no pylons. It takes it out of you.
Bring a flask. The reservoir is very pretty, and you will not want to drink it.

people.name: Surveyor
lines: The new line goes straight through here. I have put the posts in. The pylons are coming.
I have been told that by a very reliable man, who has since retired.

people.name: Warm Water Bob
lines: Lovely and warm, this. Comes out of the station like a bath. Fish love it.
They have not got as many eyes as they used to. Or they have got more. I do not count them.

people.name: Angler
lines: Why is it warm, if the turbines are off? We do not ask that here.
We have a rule about it. Well, we had. The man who made it went for a swim.

people.name: Sampler
lines: A jar a day, for the Water Board. It was clear last year. It is green this year. Next year, who knows?
I have written to them. They have sent me more jars.

people.name: Rag Man
lines: Rags, bones, bits of turbine. I go round with the cart. There is no cart. I used to go round.
That Grimer is my partner. We split it fifty-fifty, and it eats its half.

people.name: Commuter
lines: The 8:15. It is a little late this morning.
I have told the office I shall be in as soon as it comes. I am not sure they are still there.

people.name: Commuter
lines: I was here before him. I want that understood. There is a system.
No, I have never seen a bus. I have seen the sign.

people.name: Schoolgirl
lines: I am going to be late for school. I started waiting when I was seven.
I think I know most of it by now, anyway.

people.name: Gauge Reader
lines: Up a bit, down a bit. I write it in the book and I send it to the dam.
The dam sends it to me. It is very good to know somebody is on top of it.

people.name: Road Mender
lines: Three weeks I have been filling this hole. The Company is paying by the shovel.
They have not paid yet. So I dig it out, and fill it in again, to keep the shovels up.

people.name: Old Ohm
lines: The turbines stopped the year the Card Key went missing.
Last I heard it was dropped in the pines, out west.

people.name: Linesman
lines: The turbines have not turned since the flood.
The falls still try. Listen to them.

people.name: Night Watchman
lines: There is a steel shutter on the floor below.
Only the Card Key opens it, and the card was lost in the pines.

people.name: Guard
lines: The shutter takes the Card Key. The lift takes power.
Nobody gets down here by accident.

people.name: Grunt
lines: Step on an arrow and the floor carries you till something stops you.
The generator is across all that. Took me a week.

people.name: Scientist
lines: The lift only runs once the generator on the floor above is back on.
Whoever did that, thank you. I was down here a long time.

people.name: Dinner Lady
lines: Pie. It was going to be pie on the Thursday, and the Thursday has not properly finished.
Eat up. You look like the night shift.

people.name: Night Shift
lines: We are not on strike. We were asleep when they called it, and nobody has told us officially.

people.name: Branch Secretary
lines: All in favour of carrying on? Carried. It has been carried every month for nine years.
That card you are after, by the way. The Card Key. It went in the pines, with the last man who cared.

people.name: Warden
lines: Welcome to the reserve.
Pokemon live in these reeds that you will not find anywhere else in the vale.

people.name: Ticket Man
lines: One ticket, free of charge. Do not lose it. There is no way of checking it, but do not lose it.
The real gate? That was the real gate. It is just mostly a hut now.

people.name: Day Tripper
lines: We came all the way from Millbrook to see something rare.
We have seen a Rattata. Tom thinks it is a very rare Rattata.

people.name: Tom
lines: That Rattata is very rare. I can tell. It looked at me.

people.name: Reserve Warden
lines: The rest house is the only dry ground for a good way. We lose the odd visitor between huts.
The Kangaskhan by the east pond has been told not to. It is very firm about it.

people.name: Stile Warden
lines: North of here it is all the Power Station. They send us their hum, and we send them our midges.
The old Warden went to the harbour about his teeth. He left instructions. Nobody could understand them.

people.name: Stuck Birder
lines: I am perfectly all right. I came in for a closer look, in the spring.
If you are going back, tell them on the deck that it was a reed. It was a reed the whole time.

people.name: Reed Cutter
lines: I cut reeds, and they grow back, and I cut them. The Warden says it is good for the marsh.
He says hoh hoh. I have decided that is what he means.

people.name: Birder
lines: Sh. Sh. There. In the reeds. No, it has gone.
That was a Scyther. Or a reed. They are very similar in this light.

people.name: Twitcher
lines: Forty-one species from this deck. I have seen two. The other thirty-nine are in my notebook, on trust.
If you see a Dratini, do not tell me. I could not bear it.

people.name: Egg Counter
lines: Six to a cluster, three clusters, eighteen. It was eighteen this morning. It keeps being eighteen.
They are not eggs. Nobody here has the heart to tell the Warden.

people.name: Nursemaid
lines: I do not run this nursery. I work here. That one runs it, and she has views on my hands.
Chansey does the rounds. She has been here longer than the roof.

people.name: Property Clerk
lines: Whatever the marsh takes, it gives back here, in about a year, and wetter.
A gentleman asks after gold teeth every month by post. I cannot read the letters. I think they say hoh.

people.name: Tour Guide
lines: Stay together, please! We left with twelve. We are now, let me see, four, and a very good four.
On your left, reeds. On your right, reeds. There will be time for questions at the end.

people.name: Tourist
lines: It said rare and exotic in the brochure. Is that what that was?
My husband went to see about a toilet, by the second pool. On Tuesday.

people.name: Tourist
lines: Lovely. Lovely. Do they do a tea?
I am in it for the sandwiches. I am not sure anyone else on this tour is still alive.

people.name: Tourist
lines: We saw a very big one and it looked at us and Mr Dobbs is not with us now.
I am going to be a warden.

people.name: Mr Dobbs
lines: Excuse me. Is this the tour? I only stepped away for a moment.
They said to follow the flag. It was a very large flag. It may have been a Pinsir.

people.name: Pool Angler
lines: Long and blue, and it looks at you. I have seen it twice. I know how that sounds.
Nothing bites in here. Something watches, though, and I would rather that than nothing.

people.name: Wallow Hand
lines: My job is to turn them over. They like it. They do not say so, but you are still here, so.
Do not run. They cannot see you till you run. Then they cannot see anything else.

people.name: Head Ranger
lines: Two rangers for the whole marsh, and one of them is Moss, who thinks he is a Pokémon.
The east track is the quick way out. It is quick because nobody has ever told it about the reeds.

people.name: Trainee Ranger
lines: I am learning to read the tracks. These ones say Head Ranger went that way, in a hurry.
These ones say I should have gone with him.

people.name: Warden’s Wife
lines: Tea? Everybody comes in here wet and tells me about the one that got away.
Nobody has ever told me about one that stayed.

people.name: Wet Birder
lines: Three weeks I have been here, and I have a very good picture of some reeds.

people.name: Lost Uncle
lines: I was handed in on a Wednesday. They have been very good about it.
Nobody has claimed me yet. There is a form, and I am told it is in the marsh.

people.name: Auctioneer
lines: Lot forty-two, a lifeboat, one careful owner. Who will start me at something?
Everything must go. It has mostly gone once already.
calls: Sold, to the man in the sea!

people.name: Bidder
lines: I came for a porthole. I have bought nine, and something I was told was a chair.
I have no boat. I have a shed with very good views of the shed.

people.name: Dealer
lines: Silver, if you can find any. That is all that is worth the walk.
The sea took the plate. The camp took the spoons. I have a very good price on some forks.

people.name: Salvage Hand
lines: Up from the hold on the morning tide, sorted by noon, sold by two.
The launch for the islands puts in at the pier a while in. Do not ask what it carries back.

people.name: Tallyman
lines: Everything off the wreck is written down in this book. It is a very honest book.
I keep the other one at home.

people.name: Lady Pemberton
lines: We were told dinner would be at eight. It is the principle of the thing.
One does not simply leave a ship because it has stopped working.

people.name: Colonel Tate
lines: We paid until Tuesday, and I intend to have until Tuesday.
Splendid air. Bit of a list on the dining room.

people.name: Steward
lines: Dinner will be slightly delayed, madam. As it was yesterday.
I have a tin of something, and my training.

people.name: Master Pemberton
lines: Mother says we are on holiday. Father is still looking for the second funnel.
It is the best holiday we have ever had.

people.name: Beachcomber
lines: The bar to the wreck only shows at low water.
Whatever the sea throws up on it is anybody's.

people.name: Diver
lines: You can walk in now, through the side. It takes all the fun out of it.
I used to go down for this. I have kept the suit on, out of pride.

people.name: Second Mate
lines: Technically this is still a ship and I am still on watch.
If the Captain ever comes back from that harbour, tell him she is doing very well, considering.

people.name: Sightseer
lines: Is that it? It looked bigger on the postcard.
We have come all the way from the farm. Doreen wanted to see something go wrong.

people.name: Doreen
lines: Lovely. Lovely. You do not get wrecks like that now.
My mother saw the big one in the year of the eels. It had three funnels.

people.name: Postcard Man
lines: Picture of the wreck, one coin. Picture of the wreck before it was a wreck, two.
I had pictures of the storm but they all came out grey. I sell those as well.

people.name: Signalman
lines: Ship on the reef. I log it every morning. Same ship.
I did signal her. I signalled YOU ARE STANDING INTO DANGER, and she signalled THANK YOU.

people.name: Salvager's Wife
lines: Ned has been out on that wreck since the tide turned.
If you see him, tell him his tea is cold.

people.name: Big Stan
lines: It is a piano. It is in that crate. There is a man at the marsh who will give us ten for it.
A week, we have been at it. Two more days, if it stops going backwards.
calls: To me! To you! To me!

people.name: Little Stan
lines: I do the thinking. I think we should have gone by the road.
I said so on Monday. It was already in the wood by then.
calls: To you! To me! To you!

people.name: Piano Tuner
lines: They sent for me at the marsh end. I said I would come out and meet it.
It is flat. It is flat in every way a thing can be, apart from the one they need.

people.name: Spearow Man
lines: Sixty pairs on these rocks, every year. I count them. They come over and count me.
Do not wear a hat up here. Do not bring a sandwich. Do not look as though you might.

people.name: Landlady
lines: We did nicely out of that storm. I will not say we are pleased. I will say the roof is new.
The cook is off the ship. The chairs are off the ship. Do not ask about the bell.

people.name: Purser
lines: Tickets, please. All tickets to be shown. I am aware of the situation.
If you have no ticket you may pay the difference, and the difference is the whole ship.

people.name: Stowaway
lines: You have not seen me. I got on at the last port for a free ride to the islands.
It is the longest anyone has ever got away with it. I am never going home.

people.name: Ship’s Cook
lines: I do fourteen courses or I do nothing. Tonight it is nothing, with a light sauce.

people.name: Regular
lines: This used to be a decent pub. Now it has got a chandelier and I cannot see the darts.
I sit in a first-class chair and I have never been so uncomfortable.

people.name: Flood Warden
lines: The sea came over the wall and never went home.
The sandbags hold the lower streets. Most days.

people.name: Harbourmaster
lines: The sea took the lower town in one winter.
At low water you can walk the old streets to the stair.

people.name: Fish Wife
lines: Same pitch as my mother and hers. It was forty yards inland in her day.
The fish are fresher now. They just swim up.

people.name: Quay Porter
lines: Boats still come. They tie up to what used to be the Town Hall, and I carry it over.
North is the jetty and Gull Strand. Fishers go out from the elbow if you need off quick.

people.name: Young Angler
lines: Grandad says I am fishing in his bedroom.
I have caught a slipper.

people.name: Mr Ledger
lines: I still pay rates on Number Nine, Market Street.
It has a Krabby in it. I have written to the Krabby.

people.name: Mrs Tide
lines: We moved up a street. Then we moved up another. There is one more street.
Then there is the hill. I have my eye on the hill.

people.name: Old Salt
lines: Sit here on a quiet night and you can hear the church bell, under the water, ringing the hours.
It is wrong by twenty minutes. It always was.

people.name: Sandbagger
lines: Bag, stack, bag, stack. Boatswain Cragg says nobody goes down past him without a fight.
He means it kindly. He has seen what is down there. He wants it for himself.

people.name: Sand Boy
lines: My job is to fetch the sand. It comes from the beach. The beach is what the sea left.
So I am giving it back, really. I do not think it notices.

people.name: Shipwright
lines: Ten years ago I had one boat a month. Now every house on the street wants one.
I did very well out of the flood. Do not repeat that.

people.name: The Old Mayor
lines: This is the Mayor’s residence. I am the Mayor. I have not resigned.
The sea has not filed the proper forms. Until it does, I live here.

people.name: Diver Ames
lines: The cellars are all there. You just need a good breath and no sense.
Coral got the good bottles. I have got a very nice doorknob.

people.name: Salvage Woman
lines: The bottom street was the good end. Look at the state of that roof. Lovely slates.
I have been selling them back to the top street. They have no idea.

people.name: Stair Keeper
lines: The stair only shows at low water. A minute and a half in, it starts to show.
People wait for it. Then they stand on the last step and look back, and it is very quiet.

people.name: Clerk of Tides
lines: High water, low water, high water. Three hundred years in these ledgers.
There is a gap of one night, marked: see outside.

people.name: Old Mrs Dunn
lines: My husband went down to check the cellar.
I keep his dinner in the oven. It is a very good oven.

people.name: Eel Catcher
lines: Everything the marsh drains comes down this brook, and I catch it.
Eels. I catch eels. There has never been a keg in this pool, and I have told him so.

people.name: Eel Girl
lines: There is a gap in the trees past the pool. You go out that way, if a man in a hat comes.
I do not know why. Dad says it is for the eels.

people.name: Lookout Boy
lines: I am not a lookout. I just stand here and whistle if somebody comes.
That is you. Pretend I whistled.

people.name: Officer Pym
lines: Thirty years I have watched this sea for smugglers. Not one sail, and I have the logbook to prove it.
You will not get brandy like this anywhere else. It comes from somewhere. Very reasonable.

people.name: Lamp Boy
lines: One flash is the coast is clear. Two is the coast is not clear.
Mister Pym says it is for ships. He has never asked why I do it when there is no ships.

people.name: Sid
lines: Fresh fish. We are out of fish. We are always out of fish. We have silk.
I have got a very good silk haddock.

people.name: Aunt Lizzie
lines: Ask no questions and you will be told no lies. Turn your face to the wall.
My lot took a cargo to the burning island for years. The skiff off the jetty still goes, when the tide lets it.

people.name: Cooper
lines: Fish barrels. These are all fish barrels. That is the smell of fish.
A very strong fish. About forty per cent.

people.name: Stage Hand
lines: Boats come in here at night. Fishing boats. For fishing.
They fish at night, in fog, with no lamp, for kegs. I mean eels.

people.name: Skiffman
lines: The skiff runs out round the headland to Ember Isle once the tide is up. A minute in, say.
Stops when the big boat sails. After that you swim. It is not a swimming sort of water.

people.name: Old Rook
lines: The boat goes out when the tide turns, and not before.
You never saw this cove. Nobody ever has.

people.name: Boat Builder
lines: Fastest fishing boat in the vale, this. Black sails, no name.
Fish are very quick round here.

people.name: Tide Girl
lines: Things wash up on this beach, if you know when to look.
And dig. It washes up very deep, some of it.

people.name: Tallyman
lines: Forty tubs in, thirty-eight tubs out, and I shall write down forty.
Nobody has ever checked. Nobody knows there is a book.

people.name: Mrs Pym
lines: He has never once looked behind him. Thirty years.
I let them know when he has gone to bed. They bring me the good tea.

people.name: Old Gaffer
lines: Sixty years a fisherman. I have caught nineteen fish.
I paid for this whole house out of those fish.

people.name: Climber
lines: I came up for the view and the storm came with me.
Something small and pink watches from the cairn.

people.name: Cragsman
lines: The shelves go round the crags, one above the other.
The cairn is on the top. Mind the lightning.

people.name: Spelunker
lines: I am mapping the deepest floor.
Up the far passage there is daylight, and a storm.

people.name: Gravedigger
lines: You only find this place at night, by the sheep track.
The Gastly do no harm. Mostly.

people.name: Channeler
lines: I am a CHANNELER.
There are spirits up to mischief.
I sense them under the floor.

people.name: Mourner
lines: I came to pray for my dearly departed CLEFAIRY.
Sniff!

people.name: Old Whaler
lines: The lagoon is the other side of the berg. The cave under it is ice the whole way.
Once you are moving on ice you go till something stops you. Look before you step.
Our boat comes into the lagoon late, for anyone who got that far.

people.name: Ice Fisher
lines: The hole down is in the far corner, past the ice.
Stop against the right boulder and you are there. Stop against the wrong one and you go round again.

people.name: Lookout
lines: The skiff runs back to the cove till our boat sails. Half past two, and not a minute after.
Miss it and you are here till the burners go.

people.name: Charcoal Burner
lines: Our boat takes the charcoal off at twenty past three. There is room for one more.
The crater is ash all the way down, and something lives in every step of it.

people.name: Volcanologist
lines: The mountain breathes. Feel the ground? Warm.
It has not gone up in a hundred years. I am waiting.

people.name: Burners' Lad
lines: The tube runs on under the crater. Hot underfoot all the way.
MILLBROOK
Where every road in the vale starts.
MILL SQUARE
West: the Westward Road. North: the moor. East: The Crossing. South: Reedmere.
South to REEDMERE
Down the lane, past the pool and the woodcutter.
North to HIGH MOOR
Up the drove road, past the Grey Stones.
NOTICES
LOST: one coin purse, at the mill, on Tuesday. Reward. Ask nobody. They will only look for it.
FOR SALE: pond. Slightly used.
WANTED: somebody with a Cut to do Hazel’s hedge. It has been years.
MILL LANE
The mill is open. The miller is not, before noon.
THE ALLOTMENTS
Please do not eat the seedlings. This means you, Oddish.
THE ORCHARD
Pick what you like. Take what you can carry. The berries grow back.
HIGH MOOR
The drove road climbs to Moor Top, then north over the moor.
East: GREYSTONE PEAKS
North: the Grey Stones and the Moor Gate.
THE MOOR GATE
The old toll road leaves the vale here.
THE LITTLE STONES
There are nine. There were seven. Do not ask. Please put back any you borrow.
MOOR SPRING
The waters cure gout, grief and the common cold. Results may vary. They have varied.
THE SHEPHERD’S
Mind the flock. Nothing here is a sheep. We do not discuss it.
THE DROVERS’ FOLD
Shut the gate. Count the herd. Count them again. Accept the second number.
THE LOST FOLD
Nobody has brought a beast up here since the boulder came down. Everyone has meant to.
THE GREY STONES
The tor the vale is named for. The drovers touch it for luck.
THE WAYSTONES
They walked down from the tor one night. So the drovers say. Do not count them.
GREYSTONE PEAKS
The pass climbs through the cutting and round the head of the tarn.
THE TARN
The river starts here, under the summit.
THE HIGH PASTURE
Shut the gate behind you. The ponies wander.
THE PASS
Down: The Crossing. Up: the caves, the quarry and the tarn.
THE CUTTING
Driven through by hand. Do not ask whose. Falling rock: yes.
RANGER POST
Lost? Stay where you are. Somebody will be along. That somebody is also lost.
THE BOTHY
Free to all. Leave it as you found it. Please find it better than this.
GREYSTONE CAVES
Bring a lamp. If you have not brought a lamp, there is a woman who is very pleased to see you.
GANTRY’S STORES
Rope. Tea. More rope. Do not ask for anything else, she will only sell you rope.
THE GOAT TRACK
Over the hill and away, west of the pasture. Goats have right of way. They are not goats.
THE SUMMIT
Stormcrown, above you. Nobody has found a way up it from here. It only goes up from under.
THE CROSSING
Over the bridge: Bridge End. Tanglewood east, the peaks north, the strand south.
North: GREYSTONE PEAKS
East: TANGLEWOOD. South: GULL STRAND.
THE CROSSING
West: Millbrook and the Mill Square.
THE WEST BANK
Bridge ahead. Carters give way to nobody. Do not stand behind the Ponyta.
The road south
Down to Gull Strand and the sea.
THE COACH AND PONYTA
Hot food. Warm beds. Do not ask about the coach.
THE STONE YARD
Grey Stone cut to order. Statues by arrangement. Please do not sit on the statue. It is not finished.
THE ANGLERS’ STAGE
Members only. Membership is free. Fish are extra.
THE BEE GARDEN
Nothing here will sting you if you are polite. Be polite.
HERON WALK
Please keep to the boards. The herons will not. They have been told.
Nothing signposted
If you can read this you have gone wrong, or right. The burners do not mind.
TANGLEWOOD
East to the Eastern Track. Keep to the road.
WOODMEN’S STAND
Wood for The Crossing and the vale. Mind the logs. The logs do not mind you.
THE PICNIC GROUND
As far as the pond. No further. We mean it. We have told you now.
THE RING
Do not stand in it. Do not eat it. Do not ask it anything.
THE WAY OUT
Ales. Beds. No, it is not. We know. Everybody asks.
MISLAID
Pop. 14. Founded by accident. If you are looking for the road, so were we.
THE RUINED SHRINE
Please do not move the stones. They have been moved enough. Nobody knows by what.
THE WOOD MOUTH
Greystone Caves. Sign in with the tea. Sign out with the tea, if you can.
HALFWAY
Cut into the stone, very deep, by somebody who was sure.
DIRECTIONS
One Potion. All sales final. Refunds in the other direction.
THE EASTERN TRACK
East: Safari Marsh. West: back into all that. You have been warned.
THE BUG CLUB
Catch and release. Release optional. Mown on Tuesdays, by the Weedle, badly.
THE OLD OAK
No relation to the Professor. He has asked us to say so.
FORESTER’S LODGE
Official maps of Tanglewood. Correct as of the day before you bought it.
THE WINDFALLS
South: Orchard Terraces. The apples here belong to the farm. The apples disagree.
Chalked on the rock:
DOWN - THE WOOD, ONE FLOOR. DOWN - THE SEA, FOUR FLOORS.
Scratched on the rock by the hole:
COLD WIND FROM BELOW. NOBODY CAME BACK UP THIS WAY.
REEDMERE
The boardwalk goes round. The reeds go through.
THE HUMMOCK
The only dry ground for a mile. Please leave some of it for the next person.
PRIVATE POND
Not on any map. Keep out. This means you. Signed, the Owner (age nine).
THE LONG DRAIN
Dug by hand in the old days, by people who had been told it would help.
THE OLD PUMP
It drained this whole fen once. Then it rained.
THE MERE PUNT
Out to Duck Island and back. No charge. Mind the ducks. They do not mind you.
EELS
Smoked, jellied, or looked at. Ask at the stall.
MERE END
East: the staithe, the old pump and Gull Strand. West: the duck hide and the Mere Path.
THE DROWNED DUCK
Beds. Ale. No, you may not see the duck.
THE DUCK HIDE
QUIET PLEASE. The ones on the bank are real. The one in the water is a doll. Tess knows.
THE WITHY BEDS
Cut every seven years. Do not lean on them.
THE MERE PATH
West, out of the marsh. Last dry bed for a long way. Ask at the house.
NOTHING DOWN THIS PATH
Nothing at all. Certainly not a cove. Go back.
THE TURBARY
Peat for the whole marsh. Cut it, stack it, turn it, swear at it.
GULL STRAND
East: the orchards. South: the strand and the jetty.
GULL STRAND
West: Reedmere. East: the stone bridge. The cliff path goes down to the cove.
THE OLD LIGHT
Not lit since the boats got radios. Trimmed daily. Nobody has told Bertie.
THE ROPE WALK
Walk backwards. Keep walking. That is the whole of the trade.
THE SAILORS’ REST
They went out from the jetty. Some of them came back as far as this.
THE SALT PANS
Keep off the pans. Wade if you must. Do not lick anything.
THE QUAY
Fish off the boats by noon. After noon, ask the cat.
WRACKERS’ SAND
What the sea leaves is yours. What the sea wants back, it takes. Check the tide.
THE WEST ROAD
West: Gull Strand and the sea wall. East: the farm, and more work than you came for.
THE CIDER PRESS
Down the lane. Tasting by the jug. Mind the second jug.
NORTH ORCHARD
Do not climb the trees unless you are paid to. Do not get paid to.
THE COWMAN
Milk at the door. Knock loud. He is usually telling a Tauros something.
HONESTY BOX
Apples: one each. Leave what you think is fair. We have started counting.
THE DEW POND
It has never been dry and nothing runs into it. Nobody knows why. Nobody has asked it.
THE SLIP
One boat. For fishing. We have told the man from the Revenue the same.
THE SANDS
Along the sands west, the cockle path goes up through the wood.
ORCHARD TERRACES
The lane is east. The terraces are down, and the ledges are quicker.
THE LANE
East: The Wreck, on the cape. West and up: the farm.
Scratched on the wall:
THE BOULDERS UPSTAIRS MOVE. IT TAKES SOMETHING STRONG.
GREYSTONE POWER STATION
Service gate locked. Card Key holders only.
PYLON ROAD
North: along the reservoir and out of the vale.
SAFARI ZONE
South: the marsh reserve.
OFFICIAL PICKET
Do not cross. Strike now in its ninth year. Management informed. Management not found.
THE COMPANY SHOPS
Company tokens only. Company tokens no longer issued. Please ask for details.
WORKS CANTEEN
Thursday: pie. Other days: the rest of the pie.
DANGER OF DEATH
Not since the flood. But it is the principle of the thing.
ALLOTMENTS
Marrows may not be measured after dark. This means you, Mrs Watt.
GREYSTONE SAILING CLUB
Dinghy to the valve tower: ask nobody. There is nobody to ask.
PYLON ROAD
Pylons to follow. See the Surveyor.
RELAY MAST
Raise the linesmen on it and their track opens. They do not come. They do leave the gate.
TAILRACE
No swimming. No drinking. No reason given. Fishing permitted.
SETTLING POND
Everything in here is settling. Please do not stir it.
THE TIP
Property of the Company. Anything you find has already been thrown away by experts.
BUS STOP
The 8:15 to Millbrook. Timetable subject to the road existing.
GAUGE HOUSE
Water level read daily. Please do not tell the gauge.
STAFF ONLY
Plant room below. Keep the shutter locked.
ELEVATOR
Runs off the B2F generator. If it stops, switch it back on.
SAFARI MARSH
A warden's reserve. Keep to the paths; the reeds are full.
TICKETS
Free. There used to be a charge. There used to be a lot of things.
REST HOUSE
Tea. Dry socks. No catching on the furniture.
SAFARI MARSH: NORTH STILE
If you can hear a hum, you are going the wrong way. If you can hear a bite, also.
THE EGG BANK
Please do not sit on the eggs. They have been asked not to sit on you.
THE HIDE
Silence, please. Binoculars for hire. Binoculars not available.
THE NURSERY
Knock first. Then leave. Then knock from further away.
LOST PROPERTY
Boots, hats, three canoes and an uncle. Teeth: no. Stop asking.
THE GREAT POOL
No swimming. Something long has been seen. It has been seen looking back.
THE WALLOW
Rhyhorn cannot see well. They can hear you reading this.
RANGERS’ CAMP
East: the track and out. Sign in. Sign out. We count, at the end, and we are often surprised.
THE SOUTH PLANKS
South: The Wreck, through the wood. Mind the third plank. It is on its way to the sea.
THE WRECK
The liner went onto the reef in the last storm. The camp is below the cliff.
THE CAPE
The wreck is out on the reef, past the camp. The pier is east.
THE ICE RUN
The launch runs out to Frostreef on the flood tide.
It sails from 2:00 until 4:00.
LOTS 1-40
Sold as seen. Some of it has been seen by the sea for some time.
LOT 41
Deck chairs, nine. Sea damage. Some of the sea is still in them.
THE BAR
Dry at low water. It has been low water for some weeks. Nobody trusts it.
SALVAGE STAGE
Round the bow. Mind the planks. If you fall in, you are now a lot.
HOLD
Forward hold through the hole, which we did not make. We did make it bigger.
FIRST CLASS ONLY
Passengers in other classes are asked to wait on the other beach.
THE SHIP INN
Formerly The Cape. Formerly The Ship. Ask about our new cutlery.
THE VIEWPOINT
See the wreck. There is only the one. It does not do anything.
PLEASE KEEP LEFT
Piano in road.
THE SUNKEN QUARTER
The old high street. Mind the tide.
THE OLD QUAY
Fish, when there is fish. The jetty north goes to Gull Strand. Boat steps at its elbow.
NOTICE
Rates are still due on all properties, wet or dry. By order. Yours, the Borough.
UPPER STREET
Formerly Middle Street. Before that, Hill Street. The sea has been very good for the view.
THE BOATYARD
Repairs to anything that floats. Everything else we can only sympathise with.
MARKET STREET
Market on Thursdays. Bring a boat.
LOW WATER
Stair to the sea, a minute and a half after the tide turns. Do not wait for the second turn.
NOTHING DOWN THIS PATH
Still nothing. Told you.
DEFINITELY NO COVE
And if there were, it would be closed. Go home.
DANGER: CLIFFS
No steps here. No, those are not steps. Those are a landslip. Very tidy landslip.
HIS MAJESTY’S REVENUE
All landings to be declared at this office. Hours: when he is looking.
FRESH FISH
Ask for Sid. Do not ask for fish.
FISHER’S ROW
A fishing village. Look at all the nets. There is a net somewhere.
THE CUT
East to the shingle and the Sunken Quarter. Carts by night. Do not count them.
THE LANDING STAGE
For small boats, by night, in fog, for no reason.
STORMCROWN
The path climbs round the three crags to the cairn.
THE CLOUD STAIR
Over the top, and down the far side out of the storm.
Scratched deep in the rock:
NO WAY BACK BUT UP.
DROVERS' BOTHY
The drovers slept here the night before the fair.
LANTERN CROSS
Lit for the drovers coming over the fell after dark.
THE MOOR CHAPEL
Erected in the memory of the drovers and their POKéMON.
THE CORPSE ROAD
West, off the fell.
STATION MASTER'S GARDEN
Please keep to the paths.
FROSTREEF
The launch puts in on the flood tide. When the tide turns, it does not.
EMBER ISLE
The path climbs the south face to the Lava Tube. The crater is past it.
LAVA TUBE
The only way into the crater. Mind your step on the ash.
THE BLACK SANDS
The island makes its own beach. The boat is at the jetty on the west shore.

trainers.name: Scout Tam
lines: You look like you have got a minute. You have not. Battle me anyway!

trainers.name: Orchardist Bea
lines: Those are my apples, and that is my good ladder.

trainers.name: Drover Hale
lines: This road is for the herd!
Show me your Pokemon if you want to pass.

trainers.name: Breaker Finn
lines: This quarry is closed to visitors!
Unless you can break through me.

trainers.name: Hiker Pell
lines: It is all uphill from here. It was all uphill from there too. Fight me while I get my breath.

trainers.name: Walker Oona
lines: This is not on any map, this path. How did you find it? Tell me after!

trainers.name: Collier Bram
lines: I burn charcoal under the old oak. Nobody comes this far in.

trainers.name: Tapper Ines
lines: Five years that pot has been hanging, and you kicked it! Battle me!

trainers.name: Woodsman Crake
lines: Nobody comes down here. I come down here so nobody will. It is working, except for you.

trainers.name: Netter Bryn
lines: The bridge is my spot!
Let us see what you have caught.

trainers.name: Breaker Dunn
lines: I break rocks all day. Put your Pokemon down there and let us see.

trainers.name: Collier Osk
lines: Six days I have sat up with this stack. I could do with the company!

trainers.name: Bug Catcher Tam
lines: Everyone gets lost in here. That is how I catch them.

trainers.name: Woods Ranger Ash
lines: I walk every lane of this wood. I know exactly where I am. Let me prove it!

trainers.name: Caver Rudge
lines: I have been in deeper than anybody here! Fight me, or hold this rope.

trainers.name: Hiker Gorse
lines: Mind the sand. It sinks under you.

trainers.name: Collier Wyn
lines: There was coal down here once. Now there is only me.

trainers.name: Collier Dunn
lines: Do not wake the Sleeper. I have to work next to it.

trainers.name: Smuggler Gill
lines: That rope is spoken for.

trainers.name: Netter Fen
lines: The mere is mine at this hour. Fight for it!

trainers.name: Fowler Hugh
lines: You have put up every bird on the marsh. You can pay for them.

trainers.name: Bog Walker Rue
lines: I walk the bog for my health. It is terrible for my health. Battle me!

trainers.name: Raider Kit
lines: The strand is mine at low tide. Fight!

trainers.name: Orchardist Pip
lines: Paws off my apples!

trainers.name: Farmhand Bo
lines: I was told to keep the track clear. You are on the track!

trainers.name: Beachcomber Wyn
lines: Anything on this beach is mine. That includes you, until you beat me.

trainers.name: Damkeeper Volt
lines: Nobody touches the sluices but me!

trainers.name: Foreman Dray
lines: You from the Company? I was told to wait for somebody from the Company.
Well, somebody is going to answer for those pylons.

trainers.name: Grunt
lines: Who let you down here? The shutter was locked!

trainers.name: Grunt
lines: You came through the arrows? Then you can go back the same way!

trainers.name: Grunt
lines: The war room is off limits. Orders are orders!

trainers.name: Poacher Vince
lines: Never seen that Scyther before in my life. Whose sack is this? Yours, is it? It had better be.

trainers.name: Ranger Moss
lines: The ranger's track is mine to keep. Show me what you caught!

trainers.name: Salvager Ned
lines: This camp has first pick of the wreck!
You want a share, you earn it.

trainers.name: Wrecker Bess
lines: A lantern? On a cliff? I have no idea what you mean. Give me that.

trainers.name: Diver Coral
lines: I dive the mansion cellars. Finders keepers!

trainers.name: Rates Man Odd
lines: I have a bill here for every house on this street, and one for you. Settle up!

trainers.name: Grunt
lines: Hey! That cargo is spoken for!

trainers.name: Carter Mags
lines: You never saw this cart. You never saw me. You are about to not see my Pokémon!

trainers.name: Wrecker Tobin
lines: That light on the headland? That is to help the ships. Help them onto the rocks!

trainers.name: Hiker Brann
lines: Nobody climbs Stormcrown without a fight!

trainers.name: Hiker Rudd
lines: Nobody comes this deep for the view.

trainers.name: Gardener Rowan
lines: These beds were the station master's pride. Mind where you tread!

trainers.name: Smuggler
lines: Nobody comes through the tube but us!

trainers.name: Smuggler
lines: That hoard is the whole run. Hands off it!
